# Theoretical-physics review

## Overall assessment

The original identity-chart analysis was mathematically useful, but the
global wording and the antipodal interpretation overstated what had been
proved.  The revised manuscript now contains a genuine full-class-angle
theorem.  Its strongest contribution is an explicit bridge between exact
SU(2) heat-kernel formulas, finite-time arbitrary-order estimates, and a
reproducible rational specialization.

## Mathematical assessment

The character and Poisson-image normalizations agree with the generator
`(1/2) Delta` and Haar probability.  Pairing opposite images before division
removes the identity singularity, and Bell-polynomial bounds correctly
propagate finite derivative hierarchies through the logarithm once a positive
floor is established.  The transition chart no longer relies on the
order-dependent time monotonicity used near the identity: it maximizes each
`exp(-A/t)t^-r` factor exactly.

At the antipode, the relevant geometric degeneracy is an `S^2` family of
minimizing geodesics.  The two leading objects in the one-dimensional image
sum are radial affine-Weyl terms, not two geodesics.  Their removable limit
gives the correct `t^-5/2 exp(-pi^2/(2t))` leading behavior.  The cut-chart
derivative theorem is finite at each `t>0` and correctly avoids claiming
uniformity as `t -> 0`.

## Physics assessment

The revised conventions make the lattice interpretation auditable:
`T^a=sigma^a/2`, `theta=|X|/2`, and a spin-Casimir heat time `tau=2t`.
The continuum expansion is now convention-dependent in an explicit way, and
the numerical example gives a usable one-plaquette convexity/nonlinearity
budget.  These results do not yet imply an interacting plaquette marginal,
large-field control, an RG contraction, or a mass gap; the manuscript now
states those limitations directly.

## Publication recommendation

After the implemented major revision, the paper is suitable for circulation
as a focused mathematical-physics methods note.  Its claims should remain at
the SU(2), one-plaquette, finite-time enclosure level.  Any future extension
to SU(N) must address intersecting Weyl walls and cannot be presented as a
formal vector replacement of the present image sum.
